subject: Literature
title: Coriolanus and the Dangers of Democracy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Coriolanus and the Dangers of Democracy.

hook.text: A Roman war hero despises the common people so openly that they banish him, and he joins the enemy.

buildup.text: Coriolanus refuses to perform humility before voters, seeing democratic rituals as degrading and dishonest.

discovery.text: Shakespeare gave both sides compelling arguments: the elite's competence versus the people's right to a voice.

twist.text: Both fascists and communists have staged the play as propaganda, each claiming it supports their own ideology.

climax.text: Coriolanus remains the sharpest dramatic examination of populism, elitism, and democratic tension ever written.

punchline.text: Both dictators and democrats claim this play as theirs.

quiz.question: Why is Coriolanus politically unusual among Shakespeare's plays?
options: It has no political content at all
Both fascists and communists have staged it as supporting their own ideology
It is Shakespeare's only play set in ancient Rome
